title: Ecosystem Accords have indefinite duration and can only be terminated or modified by an Atlas Edit
content:
Every Accord in this chunk states an indefinite duration with a commencement date and nothing else: Keel from June 23 2025 (A.2.8.2.3.1.2), Obex from November 13 2025, Core Council Executor Agent 1 from December 11 2025, Osero from December 18 2025, Skybase from September 1 2024, Amatsu and Ozone from March 19 2026. Grove's (A.2.8.2.10.1.2) is the most explicit: indefinite, commencing **retroactively** from July 24 2025, and "remains in effect unless terminated or modified via an Atlas Edit."

Two consequences follow. First, there is no scheduled review — an Accord that stops making sense does not lapse, it must be actively repealed, and repeal costs the same governance effort as any other Atlas change. The default is continuation.

Second, the amendment route being an Atlas Edit means the agreement *is* the Atlas text. There is no separate signed instrument that the Atlas merely summarizes; changing the words in A.2.8.2.x changes the parties' obligations. This is why Accord subdocuments can carry operative language like "Sky Governance hereby consents" (A.2.8.2.7.2.2.3.1) — the Atlas is executing, not reporting.

Grove's retroactive commencement shows the same machinery used to legitimize a relationship that already existed in practice: the Accord documents a live arrangement backdated to its real start, rather than restarting it.
description: No expiry, no renewal cycle, no unilateral exit: the Accord persists until governance amends the Atlas text itself, which makes the Atlas the contract registry rather than a description of
